trial_court: IV Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru (CCH−21), OS. No.25640/2017
case_name: Smt. Savithramma vs Smt. Manjula Bai

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Manjula Bai, second wife; Rama Bai and Sri.S.Krishna Rao, children

facts_of_case: Plaintiff seeks partition of suit schedule properties and separate possession of half share; defendants are second wife and children of deceased husband.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the plaintiff to prove her case.
legal_principles.held: On considering the pleadings, oral and documentary evidence of the parties, at the outset, it is worth to note, it is specific case of the plaintiff that, she is legally wedded wife of Late.Sri.K.Subba Rao.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not entertain a claim that is based on false or fabricated evidence.
legal_principles.held: Such being so, the plaintiff in order to grab the properties of these defendants,she is falsely claiming that she is legally wedded of wife Late.Sri.K.Subba Rao, infact she is not at all a wife of said Late. Sri.K.Subba Rao.

outcome.final_order: The court granted the plaintiff's prayer for partition and separate possession of half share in the suit schedule properties.
